walkthroughs.body_html:
Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are urbanisation rates currently higher in LICs than HICs?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
LICs have higher urbanisation rates because they have more cities than HICs.
HICs urbanised earlier and are now near saturation (80%+ urban); LICs are still in the rapid urbanisation phase, with high rural-urban migration and urban natural increase.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between random, stratified and systematic sampling?
options: Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
All three sampling methods produce the same results.

Random: every member has equal chance of selection. Systematic: pick every nth item. Stratified: divide the population into groups and sample proportionally from each — ensures subgroup representation.

mcqs.q: What happens at a constructive (divergent) plate boundary?
options: At constructive boundaries the plates collide and build mountains.
Plates move apart, magma rises to fill the gap and solidifies, forming new oceanic crust — for example at the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.
At constructive boundaries the plates slide past each other sideways.
